correctness.rationale: For the 16-vertex G(8,3), the standalone checker exhaustively verifies each radius-two edge-neighborhood union is the complement of the antipodes of its endpoints and the antipodal edge set is again the 24 original edges. This establishes an exact scale-five Alexander-dual equality. Acyclicity of 542 disjoint simplicial Morse pairs is confirmed by a complete 1,090-vertex/4,272-incidence topological sort; exact integer boundary cancellations along all 542 unit pivots leave one critical 0-cell, four 3-cells and one 4-cell with zero differential, so integral cohomology is free. The 16-vertex Alexander-duality shift j ↔ 13-j gives ranks one in degree 9 and four in degree 10. At radius four all 16 maximal 9-simplices have mutually intersecting vertex sets of size at most seven, proving the top boundary is injective; smaller radii have dimension ≤5. At radius six every missing-single-vertex facet occurs, hence ∂Δ15=S14; radius seven yields the full simplex. These exact facts prove all j≥9 persistent bars. Independent mod-two chain ranks corroborate the finite reduction, not replace its integral proof.

value.rationale: The Möbius–Kantor graph is a canonical cubic symmetric graph with 16 vertices and diameter four; its near-terminal graph Čech filtration is a geometrically motivated object, not an arbitrary parameter slice. The exact identification with an independence Alexander dual explains a sharp jump from zero degree-9/10 homology through two successive high-dimensional phenomena and a complete j≥9 integral barcode. This structural bridge gives a reproducible benchmark for late-scale graph Čech persistence and detects high-degree classes that the graph itself lacks. The 14-dimensional sphere at the next scale is conceptually different from the 9- and 10-dimensional classes it replaces. Prior exact independence homotopy is recognized; mathematical interest is in the metric-filtration bridge and birth/death classification, not in recomputation alone.
